evidence.quote: match LocalSnapshot.decode snapshot with ... | Ok restored when not restored.Problems.IsEmpty -> failed (first restored.Problems)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new domain rules sit in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer decides whether a transfer file is acceptable: schema, version, snapshot checks and data-version match. The engine (Summa.Web.Engine, Tier 2) decides which books may be replaced (the 'already hold records' predicate), the GitHub refusal and the files-pack refusal. The only Tier 3 change is in AccountingWire, which maps the three kernel events to engine messages and decides nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with
use stream = new MemoryStream() ... use w = new Utf8JsonWriter(stream)

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is performed below Tier 4. The clock comes in through ctx.Now. The download is returned as an OfferDownload effect value, and the import's save goes through the existing `save` path (a SaveBooks effect), so the edge carries both out. Transfer.fs uses System.IO.MemoryStream and System.Text.Json for in-memory serialization. That breaks the instance's ARC-SYM-01 symbol rule for Tier 2, but it reads no file, clock or network and writes nothing outside memory, so it is not an effect under AR-09.

evidence.quote: | _, _, false -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most facts point to one existing authority: the data version (Exports.dataVersion), the classification (Exports.Classification), the snapshot encoding (LocalSnapshot.encode/decode), the business date for the file name (Organization.businessDate), and the Schema/Version literals. Two things are copied, and the copies agree today. The file's timestamp format is written out separately in the writer (stamp) and the reader (exportedAt) instead of sharing one constant, and the 'cannot offer downloads' sentence is copied from the existing download branch at line 2838.

evidence.quote: | Ok actual, Some expected, Some _ when actual = expected && version = 2 && claimed root <> Some(contents restored.Books) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The contents count and the contents-match refusal are in Summa.Storage.Transfer (Tier 2). The preview is in the engine's view projection (Tier 2) and asks Transfer.read and Transfer.contents rather than working anything out again. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code changes, apart from index.html binding the view value.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added. The preview is a pure function of the pasted text, computed in the view projection. The new contents writing and reading is in-memory JSON inside Transfer.fs, with no I/O, clock or randomness.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The contents count has one definition (Transfer.contents), and export, read and the preview all use it. The current version number is restated, though. `Version` is set to 2, but the reader matches the literal `1 | 2` and switches on the literal `version = 2` instead of referring to `Version`, so the two would drift on the next bump. The export-date formatting is also a copy of the one used for the import notice in change set 1. All copies agree today.
